title: Confirm each pick and report the stock-out as the lamps call the bins in turn
instruction: Pick the order shown by the lamps into the order tote, one bin at a time: take one part for every lit green lamp from the lit bin, then press its white confirm button to light the next bin; if the lit bin is empty, press its red shortage button instead and take nothing in its place; stop when every lamp is dark.
context: On sequenced pick-to-light lines the next pick lights only after the last is confirmed, so the picker keeps reading the rack. An unconfirmed pick stalls the order, and a silent substitute for a stock-out ships a wrong one. Unlike kitting from a static display (TK-VN35AJ), where every lit bin shows at once and only the finished kit is judged, here each pick is confirmed in turn, and a stock-out must be reported.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y left; heights from the table top (74.75 cm above the floor). Bins: four fixed dark grey plastic parts bins at x = 34, y = 15, 5, -5 and -15 (yellow, grey, orange, blue), each 9 x 9 cm inside with 1 cm walls rising 3 cm above the table and a 0.6 cm floor (neighbours share a wall). A stocked bin holds three identical parts standing at x = 31, 34 and 37: yellow or orange plastic cylinders (2.6 cm diameter, 3.5 cm tall, 50 g), or grey or blue painted-wood blocks (2.5 x 2.5 x 3.5 cm, 60 g). Lamps: a fixed dark grey plastic strip (2.5 along x, 41 along y, 1 cm tall) centred at (27, 0); on it two 2.5 cm cubes per bin at the bin's y + 2 (left) and y - 2 (right), glowing bright green when lit, else dark. One bin is lit at a time. Buttons: per bin a white confirm plunger at the bin's y + 2 and a red shortage plunger at y - 2, plastic, 4 x 1.4 x 1.4 cm, 15 g, lying on the table with its front face at x = 21; each slides along x between two fixed dark grey rails (3 x 0.4 x 0.8 cm, x 22.75 to 25.75, 1 cm either side of the plunger's centre) and stops against the strip after 7.5 mm; no spring. Orders (one per trial; three bins lit in turn, with lamps lit; the second is always empty, its parts removed): A: yellow 2, orange 1 (empty), blue 1. B: blue 2, grey 1 (empty), yellow 1. C: orange 1, grey 2 (empty), blue 2. The screenshot shows A at its start. Tote: a fixed blue plastic order tote at (11, 0), 10 x 14 cm inside, 1 cm walls rising 4 cm above the table, 0.4 cm floor.
scoring: Terms. In the tote: centre inside the tote's walls and at most 5 cm above their tops (stacked or held counts). Placed: in the tote, at rest (under 1 cm/s), underside within 1 cm of its floor (so three parts lie on the floor, not stacked), and each gripper's fingertip midpoint 2 cm or more from the part. Pressed: a plunger moved 4 mm or more from its start. Only pushing it in, toward the strip, can count as right; pulling it out or forcing it from its rails is a wrong press. Each button counts once, stays counted even if pulled back, and can't be redone, so a bin whose button was pressed while dark can then be passed only with its other button. One bin is lit at a time; a press on the lit bin's button dims it and lights the next, a press on any other bin changes nothing. Points (6 in every order, read at the end of the trial): each placed part up to its bin's lamps in the order; each stocked bin's confirm, if the tote held exactly its lit count from that bin when it was pressed while the bin was lit; the empty bin's shortage while it was lit. Wrong: each part in the tote beyond its bin's lamps (any substitute); each bin with a part in the tote while dark and not yet done, whether it lights later or never (latched: taking the part out doesn't clear it, and a substitute left in counts under this and the rule before); each part on the floor; every other press (a confirm at any other count or on the empty bin, a shortage on a stocked bin, any press on a bin that isn't lit). Score, in order: 1.0 for every point with nothing wrong (the trial ends once this holds 1 s); with nothing wrong, points / available; with anything wrong, (points - 2 x wrong) / available, at most 0.2 and not below 0, so pressing every button scores 0. An extra part from a lit bin stops counting once it is out of the tote. A part knocked out of its bin onto the table counts neither way. The task's score is the mean over one trial of each order. On real arms: an operator switches the lamps on seeing the lit bin's plunger reach 4 mm; count the tote's parts from a top-down photo after the arms withdraw, and note each press, and the tote's count then, from the video.
reset_notes: Stand the parts back in their bins, slide every button out to its start (front face at x = 21), and set the next order (A, B, C in turn): light its first bin's lamps and take the empty bin's three parts out.
fidelity: Approximate. The lamps are glowing coloured cubes switched by the scorer's order state; the quantity is one lamp per unit, not a digit. The buttons are free plungers sliding in rails with no spring or switch; the scorer records each press. Three fixed orders, chosen at the start, not by an order system. Parts are plain shapes. Loose objects have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
